basis: Mesocestoides tapeworm infection usually occupies the intestine; extraintestinal disease is uncommon in humans.
Acute alveolar-capillary injury causes pulmonary edema and respiratory failure; associated sepsis and systemic complications do not establish additional direct organ disease.
Inherited pyrimidine metabolism disorder; this subtype explicitly lacks megaloblastic anemia. No other common organ damage is established.
Metabolic myopathy with episodic muscle breakdown and myoglobinuria; acute renal failure is occasional and excluded.
VZV infection causes characteristic cutaneous infection in chickenpox and shingles; persistent neurologic injury is not common across the umbrella.
Congenital small-bowel obstruction and hypoplasia define the disease; mesenteric vascular disruption explains the bowel defect without establishing separate vascular disease.
Carcinoma originates in the rete testis, a reproductive structure outside the axes; endocrine gonadal disease is not established.
Severe neurodevelopmental disease and sensorineural deafness define the syndrome; optic atrophy occurs in 2/6 and strabismus in 5/6.
Clonal blood and marrow neoplasm, often involving the spleen; no additional organ has established damage in at least 30%. Cardiac fibrosis is described as rare.
Corneal opacity, elbow contractures with forearm bone abnormalities, and intellectual/developmental impairment are defining, very frequent features.
Defining limb, ectodermal and oral defects; lacrimal stenosis 6/6. Four-axis cap excludes less consistent urinary and ear abnormalities.
Malignancy originates in cutaneous eccrine sweat glands.
Glycosylation disorder with defining joint contractures and skin fragility; retinal detachment occurs in 30-79%. Bruising reflects tissue fragility, not a blood disorder.
Corynebacterial infection of the fauces/pharyngeal airway; toxin-related cardiac or neurologic complications do not meet the common-involvement threshold.
Suppurative inflammation of lymph nodes, usually caused by bacterial infection; no blood-cell or marrow disease is established.
Developmental impairment, congenital heart defects and cleft palate define the phenotype; asplenia occurs in 1/2. Minor skeletal anomalies omitted at the four-axis cap.
Broad collagen/connective-tissue disorder umbrella; skeletal involvement is shared, while ocular, vascular and immune disease depend on subtype.
Ependymal tumor originates in the spinal cord.
Localized hepatic inflammatory mass with IgG4-related lymphoplasmacytic infiltration and fibrosis; systemic organ involvement is not established for this concept.
In situ carcinoma originates in the extrahepatic bile duct, included in the hepatic axis.
Microcephaly and developmental delay occur in 2/2 reported patients; chromosomal instability and cancer susceptibility do not themselves establish other organ damage.
Paget carcinoma affects anal/perianal squamous epithelium, encompassing anal canal and skin forms; associated colorectal cancer is a separate malignancy.
Neurodevelopmental impairment is the predominant phenotype; cardiac, ocular and skeletal defects are occasional, below 30%.
Inherited congenital heart malformations define the disease; no other organ involvement is supplied.
Carpenter skeletal malformations define disease; patent ductus arteriosus and cutis laxa each occur in 2/5. Developmental delay and hearing loss each occur in only 1/5.
